prompt: Why should the set's tests never be skipped?

choices.text: They call no model and cost nothing
choices.why: Right. And they catch a broken manifest or a customer's name in seconds.

choices.text: They are the only tests that use Presidio
GitHub requires them on every pull request
choices.why: GitHub requires nothing of the kind.

choices.text: They take the longest to run

prompt: What can a pipeline not do in the third tier?

choices.text: Schedule the held-out run
Call a judge model
Read the replies that changed
choices.why: Right. That is a person's job.

prompt: Why do production and the candidate answer the set in the same run?

choices.text: It halves the cost of the gate
pytest cannot read a stored run
Production changes on every commit
Any drift shows in both runs
choices.why: Right. A model or price that changed cancels out; a stored baseline would blame the candidate.

prompt: Which way of losing a gate does this section call the most common?

choices.text: A test with too weak an assertion
A test that quietly did not run
choices.why: Right: a missing variable, a forgotten skip.

choices.text: A budget set too high
A set with too few cases

prompt: 2026.10.4's latency budget passed on one run and failed on another, with nothing changed. What follows?

choices.text: A budget near the noise passes at random
choices.why: Right. Widen it past the noise, or measure more requests.

choices.text: Rerun the gate until the budget passes
choices.why: A gate rerun until it passes is a gate that passes.

choices.text: Latency cannot be given a budget at all
choices.why: It can, wider than the noise.

choices.text: The machine was broken on the slower run
choices.why: Nothing was broken; a median over 32 replies moves.
